description: Hi! We are Bozkır, and we're excited to be part of NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026! We're interested in exploring how technology, AI, and space data can help solve real-world problems, especially in agriculture. We enjoy learning new things, exchanging ideas, and getting creative with technology. We're looking forward to meeting new people, working together, and having fun while creating something meaningful!
summary: BOZKIR is an interactive, web-based crop rotation decision-support platform that transforms NASA POWER historical climate data into practical agricultural insights. Choosing what to plant next requires balancing crop diversity, climatic conditions, and water-related considerations. However, accessing and interpreting historical climate data can be challenging for farmers and agricultural planners. BOZKIR addresses this challenge by connecting location-based climate analysis with crop water indicators and transparent crop rotation comparisons. Users can register their fields, explore historical rainfall and temperature patterns, estimate crop evapotranspiration, and compare alternative crop sequences through an intuitive interface. By combining NASA Earth data with established agricultural calculation methods and explainable decision rules, BOZKIR makes climate-informed agricultural planning more accessible. Our goal is to help users understand the potential trade-offs between different crop rotation strategies and explore more informed, climate-aware farming decisions.
details:
The Challenge

Agricultural planning is becoming increasingly complex as farmers face changing climatic conditions and growing pressure on water resources. Choosing an appropriate crop rotation requires considering several factors, including crop diversity, botanical family relationships, seasonal climate conditions, and crop water requirements. Although historical climate datasets are publicly available, transforming these datasets into understandable information for agricultural planning remains challenging. BOZKIR was developed to bridge this gap between Earth data and practical crop rotation planning.

Our Solution

BOZKIR is an interactive web-based decision-support application that combines NASA POWER historical meteorological data with agricultural calculation methods and transparent crop rotation evaluation rules. Users can register agricultural fields, select their geographic locations, explore historical climate patterns, define crop growth scenarios, and compare alternative crop rotation strategies. Instead of presenting a single unexplained recommendation, BOZKIR provides comparative indicators and explanations so users can understand how different factors influence the results.

 

How Does It Work?

1. Field Registration and Location Selection

Users create field profiles by entering a field name, area, current crop, and irrigation type. They select the field location directly on an interactive map. The selected coordinates are used to retrieve location-specific climate information.

2. Historical Climate Analysis with NASA POWER

BOZKIR retrieves daily historical meteorological data from NASA POWER for the selected coordinates. BOZKIR analyzes historical precipitation and temperature records beginning in 2005, using available and complete NASA POWER data:

  • Average annual precipitation
  • Average temperature
  • Annual rainfall variability
  • Historical annual rainfall patterns
  • Average monthly temperature patterns

These visualizations provide climate context for agricultural planning. They represent historical data rather than future weather forecasts.

3. Reference Evapotranspiration Calculation

To estimate atmospheric water demand, BOZKIR implements the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith method for calculating reference evapotranspiration (ETo).

The calculation uses meteorological inputs retrieved from NASA POWER, including temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, solar radiation, and surface pressure.

The backend processes these inputs and calculates daily ETo values in millimeters per day.

 

4. Crop Water Indicator Estimation

BOZKIR applies the FAO-56 single crop coefficient approach to estimate crop evapotranspiration (ETc). ETc is calculated using:

  • ETc = Kc × ETo

Crop coefficients vary across the initial, development, mid-season, and late-season growth stages. Users can define planting dates and adjust crop growth-stage durations and coefficient assumptions. The application also compares estimated crop evapotranspiration with gross historical precipitation to generate preliminary water-related screening indicators. These indicators are not equivalent to irrigation requirements because effective rainfall, soil-water storage, runoff, drainage, and irrigation efficiency are not yet modeled. 

5. Crop Rotation Comparison

Users can compare three crop sequences:

  • Current Rotation
  • Alternative A
  • Alternative B

The application evaluates rotation structure using transparent rules that consider:

  • Crop diversity
  • Botanical family diversity
  • Legume inclusion
  • Repetition of the same crop in consecutive years
  • Repetition of crops from the same botanical family

Water-related screening indicators are also calculated for the selected crop scenarios.

 

6. Adjustable Evaluation Priorities

Users can choose between three evaluation priorities:

  • Balanced: 50% rotation structure and 50% water screening
  • Water Priority: 30% rotation structure and 70% water screening
  • Rotation Diversity Priority: 70% rotation structure and 30% water screening

The application combines these weighted indicators into a comparative prototype score. This approach allows users to explore how different priorities affect the ranking of alternative crop sequences.

Benefits and Expected Impact

BOZKIR aims to make climate information more accessible and useful for agricultural planning. Its main benefits include:

  • Transforming NASA POWER historical climate data into understandable visual information.
  • Helping users explore the relationship between climate conditions and crop water indicators.
  • Enabling comparisons between alternative crop rotation sequences.
  • Making evaluation criteria and weighting choices transparent.
  • Providing an accessible starting point for climate-informed agricultural planning.

Our Goal

Our goal is to bridge the gap between satellite-supported Earth data and everyday agricultural decision-making. We hope to make climate-informed crop rotation exploration easier for farmers, agricultural students, researchers, and agricultural planners. BOZKIR is designed to support human decision-making, not replace local agronomic expertise.

 

Development Approach

We developed a Python-based backend to retrieve NASA POWER data, process meteorological inputs, calculate evapotranspiration indicators, and evaluate crop rotation scenarios. A React-based frontend provides field management, interactive climate visualizations, crop calendar configuration, and comparative rotation results. Throughout development, we focused on making the calculations understandable, the evaluation rules transparent, and the interface accessible.
